Heatmap: Interactive heatmap of harmonized UPS protein expression across 20 tissue types and 10 CPTAC tumor cohorts. Select E3 ligases, DUBs, or other UPS components to visualize tissue-specific expression patterns. This analysis integrates data from CPTAC, PRIDE, TPCPA, and CCLE (González-Robles et al., Figure 6).
Boxplot: Compare UPS protein expression across tumor types and normal tissues. This module enables identification of tumor-specific UPS dysregulation, including upregulation of oncogenic E3s like SKP2 and DTL, or downregulation of tumor suppressors like PRKN (González-Robles et al., Figure 2).
Density Plots: Visualize the distribution of UPS protein abundance across cancer cohorts using kernel density curves. Useful for identifying expression outliers and understanding the dynamic range of E3 ligase or DUB expression in different tumor contexts.
Volcano Plots: Differential expression analysis (tumor vs normal) showing log2 fold-change vs -log10(FDR). Identifies significantly dysregulated UPS components across CPTAC cohorts. Our analysis revealed 410 E3 ligases with significant alterations in at least one tumor type (González-Robles et al., Figure 2).
Heatmap Cancer Subtypes: Explore how UPS protein expression varies across cancer molecular subtypes. This analysis controls for tumor purity and reveals subtype-enriched E3 ligases that may represent lineage-specific dependencies (González-Robles et al., Methods).
Heatmap Immune Subtypes: Stratify UPS expression by immune subtype classification to identify E3 ligases and DUBs associated with distinct immune microenvironments. Helps uncover immune-context-dependent proteostasis vulnerabilities.
Pancan Gene vs Gene: Spearman correlation analysis between E3 ligases and their putative substrates across pan-cancer cohorts. Enables exploration of E3-substrate co-regulation patterns and identification of mutation-associated E3 rewiring (González-Robles et al., Figure 5).
Pancan Gene vs all: Compute pan-cancer Spearman correlations between a selected UPS protein and all quantified proteins. Set correlation thresholds and highlight known BioGRID interactors to discover novel E3-substrate relationships and co-dependency networks.
Pancan Gene Panel: Generate a correlation heatmap for multiple UPS proteins simultaneously. Useful for mapping co-expression networks of E3 ligases, DUBs, and their regulatory targets across cancer types and normal tissues.
LSCC Ubiquityl: Explore ubiquitylation site-specific data from lung squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC). Correlate E3 ligase expression with ubiquitylation levels of specific lysine residues on candidate substrates, revealing E3-mediated post-translational regulation.
Oncoplot: Visualize somatic mutation landscape across CPTAC cohorts. Many UPS components harbor recurrent mutations, including tumor suppressors VHL (8%) and FBXW7 (4%), and emerging drivers like RNF213 (5%) (González-Robles et al., Figure 4D).
Lollipop: Map mutation positions along protein domains to identify recurrent hotspots in UPS genes. Visualizes consequences of somatic variants on E3 ligase structure and function, highlighting loss-of-function mutations in tumor suppressors.
QTL Analysis: Protein quantitative trait locus (pQTL) analysis linking cancer driver mutations to UPS protein remodeling. We identified 17,925 significant mutation-protein associations, revealing how TP53 loss upregulates DTL and CDC20 while downregulating DDB2 and FBXO22 (González-Robles et al., Figure 4).
CCLE Drug Sensitivity: Correlate UPS protein expression with drug response profiles from PRISM and CCLE screens. Identify therapeutic vulnerabilities associated with E3 ligase abundance, such as increased sensitivity to DNA damage agents in UBR5-high tumors (González-Robles et al., Figure 5).
CPTAC Survival: Survival analysis stratifying patients by UPS protein abundance (high vs low quartiles). We identified 153 E3 ligases associated with overall survival, including pan-cancer predictors (FBXL18, FBXL3) and lineage-specific prognostic markers (González-Robles et al., Figure 3).
Download Data: Access processed CPTAC, CCLE, PRIDE, and TPCPA datasets, including harmonized UPS protein expression matrices, mutation calls, sample metadata, gene lists, and correlation matrices. All data used in González-Robles et al. are available for offline analysis.
